subtype: Approach: seek support and review habits afterwards [Revision]
passage:
Dear Akash,

You asked how I am, and typing "fine" felt wrong, so here is the real answer. Two weeks ago I skidded on gravel riding home at eleven at night. My shoulder is bruised and the headaches kept coming back after dark. I finally told Mum and Dad everything on Sunday, and Dad took me to the doctor, who checked me over. I'm going back for a follow-up next week.

I have made new rules and taped them next to my helmet shelf: strap the helmet on every single ride, stay under the limit even when friends pull ahead, and no riding after nine at night. I'll take the bus instead. It feels like giving up some freedom, but it also feels like the fall taught me something. Come over and I'll tell you the whole story.

Aparna

qa.q: Which rules did Aparna tape next to the helmet shelf?
qa.a: Strap the helmet on every ride, stay under the limit, and no riding after nine at night.

qa.q: How does Aparna feel about the new rules?
qa.a: Aparna's feelings are mixed: it feels like giving up some freedom, but Aparna also feels the fall taught something useful.

qa.q: What else could Aparna do to make the new habits last, and why?
qa.a: Aparna could ask Akash or a friend to check in on the rules and keep the follow-up visit, because support makes new habits easier to keep.

qa.q: How might Aparna's parents have felt on hearing everything on Sunday?
qa.a: They were probably worried and also relieved that Aparna finally told them, since it let Dad take Aparna to the doctor.

grounding: Illustrates a shaken person talking with family, seeing a doctor and adopting stricter rules on helmets, speed and night riding.
